solution: So $c=\cos40^\circ,\cos80^\circ,\cos160^\circ$ are the roots of $8c^3-6c+1=0$ (distinct, so all three roots)
solution_full: So $c=\cos\theta$ satisfies $4c^3-3c=-\dfrac12$, i.e. $8c^3-6c+1=0$. The three values $\cos40^\circ$, $\cos80^\circ$, $\cos160^\circ$ are distinct, so they are exactly the three roots.
Put $u=\dfrac1c=\sec\theta$: dividing $8c^3-6c+1=0$ by $c^3$ gives $8-6u^2+u^3=0$, i.e. $u^3-6u^2+0\cdot u+8=0$.
originality_note: New: the sum of CUBES of secants with a sign pattern, obtained by recognising 40, 80, 160 degrees as the three solutions of cos 3theta = -1/2 and using Newton's sum for the reciprocal cubic (way 5). Closest known: sec^2 20 + sec^2 40 + sec^2 80 = 36 and sec 40 + sec 80 - sec 20 = 6. Different because: the cubic power sum needs e1, e2, e3 of the reciprocal equation, and the sign of sec 160 must be handled.

concept_use.Compound angles: sin(A+/-B), cos(A+/-B),: cos 3theta = cos(2theta + theta) expansion builds the cubic; the roots are theta, 120 - theta, 120 + theta type angles.
concept_use.Multiple angles: ratios of 2A and 3A: cos 3theta = 4cos^3 theta - 3 cos theta = -1/2 for theta = 40, 80, 160 degrees gives the cubic 8c^3 - 6c + 1 = 0.
